summary: This turn closes the remaining source-level link in the reframed StopSign account. The end state shows leader 4 without the marker even though its prepare quorum merged a StopSign-bearing promise and its accepted index rose to 37, so the marker must have been removed afterwards. sync_log provides that path directly: when the applied log_sync carries a StopSign it stores it and adds one to the accepted index, but when the applied log_sync carries none while the node already holds a StopSign it clears the stored marker and records a SetStopsign(None) operation. Any later sync built from a leader or peer whose log lacks the StopSign therefore erases the marker on a node that had accepted it, which matches the observed Some to None transition on leader 4 while node 3 keeps Some. The update registers the clearing branch as a source-backed behavior and links it to the run-13 end state, with the explicit caveat that the receipt does not record which particular sync performed the erasure. Together with the earlier records, the account now covers the executed split between node 3 and leader 4, the sequence-expected Decide clamping that keeps node 3 at decided 37, the leader's decision at 38 from reported accepted indices, and the harness's divergence check that cannot see a StopSign-versus-value difference. No execution is requested. The work closes with all six registered questions explained and the StopSign family documented across its observed, constructed and source-backed parts.
